hits.name: Dr. Rhonda Patrick
hits.text: The dirty little secret about magnesium supplements - 400 mg of magnesium citrate is not 400 mg of magnesium. Magnesium citrate contains both magnesium and citrate. A label listing only “magnesium citrate, 400 mg” gives the weight of the entire compound, not the elemental magnesium dose, and can make the dose look much larger than it is. A clear label should read something like: “Magnesium (as magnesium glycinate), 120 mg, 29% Daily Value.” Magnesium also has an established Daily Value. If the panel says otherwise, that’s another red flag, and a reason to check the labels on your other mineral supplements, too!
hits.draft_en:
Dirty little secret: 400 mg of “magnesium citrate” is not 400 mg of magnesium.

That’s the whole compound. Elemental magnesium is the number that matters — and a clear label says so with a Daily Value %.

I’m 63. I don’t need a bigger bottle. I need an honest one.

Flip the label this week. If it’s fuzzy, put it back.
hits.video_tip: 25–35s phone on two bottles; point at elemental Mg line vs compound weight; caption “read the elemental dose.”

hits.name: Nick Norwitz MD PhD
hits.text: The article “The Surprising Science of an All-Meat Diet,” which I published last week, is now on the most-read list for health articles and uptrending. This morning, I also finished an interview with a major newspaper in the United Kingdom that was interested in covering my perspective on saturated fat and cholesterol for National Cholesterol Month in the UK. A brief summary of my two major positions, because I don’t think they’re at all radical. I’ll be as concise as possible and link to more information below. 1) First, the carnivore diet is a tool, not a religion. It’s a mistake to present it as the best diet for humans or to make strong claims that go beyond the literature, such as that it will improve longevity. What we can say, accurately and humbly, is that it’s helping many people who have struggled with debilitating disorders and failed to find support through conventional approaches. We can also say that there is strong biological plausibility for many of the conditions for which it’s being used, including mental health disorders and autoimmune and inflammatory conditions. That’s not definitive proof. But it’s a possibility that deserves curiosity and compassion, not disdain. If you want the full scientific breakdown in video form: “The Strange Science of Eating Only Meat” youtu.be/WJnPDQ0XRXA 2) The second major point I’ll make is that CONTEXT matters. Meat is vilified largely because of its saturated fat and cholesterol content. However, when it comes to improving the cardiometabolic health of the general population, focusing on reducing saturated fat intake is like worrying about a mosquito when you’re being chased by a tiger. We now have randomized controlled trial data showing that low-carbohydrate ketogenic diets (despite typically being much higher in saturated fat and cholesterol) can provide greater improvements in many cardiometabolic risk markers than low-fat plant-based or Mediterranean-style diets higher in carbohydrates, particularly in people with obesity and insulin resistance. More here: staycuriousmetabolism.substack.com/p/a-major-tria … At the end of the day, I don’t fancy myself a carnivore fanboy. Just carnivore-curious and open-minded. That’s enough. P.S. There’s a tendency to make meat and diet unnecessarily political. Resist that tendency. What’s on my plate does not inform what I do at the ballot box. Stereotypes impair our ability to have thoughtful academic discourse. Ht/ @MikhailaFuller for her contribution (including the click-boost from her adorable baby) @EpochTimes
hits.draft_en:
Carnivore is a tool, not a religion. Norwitz said it again and the piece keeps climbing.

Context matters. Obsessing over one fat while ignoring waist, insulin, and strength is mosquito-vs-tiger stuff.

I’m a meat-and-fruit pragmatist. Use what works. Drop the tribe war. Keep bloodwork honest.
hits.video_tip: 15–20s plate of meat/fruit; caption “tool, not tribe.”

hits.name: Benjamin Bikman
hits.text: Alcohol is a hot topic (and an odd one for a guy like me to bring up--I've never had a drop in my life). But there is a relevant metabolic angle to it. If you drink most nights while trying to lose fat, you are regularly shutting down fat oxidation. The body clears alcohol first--it's a fuel that demands "priority boarding". While that is happening, fat burning drops hard, and more of the fat from your meals gets stored instead of burned. In one study, subjects drank about 96 g of alcohol in a day (roughly seven drinks), and 24-hour fat burning fell by about a third. That drop showed up whether the alcohol was added on top of their meals or swapped in for other calories. If you're looking to lose fat, I'd put alcohol at the top of the list of things to scrutinize. pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1545851/
hits.draft_en:

Bikman’s point: drink most nights while “trying to lose fat” and you’re regularly shutting oxidation down — study showed about a third drop in 24-hour fat burn at heavy intake.

hits.name: Nick Norwitz MD PhD
hits.text: Diet Soda Debate: What Everyone (Still) Gets Wrong I recently posted some short-form content about "what everybody gets wrong about diet soda." As not only anticipated, but intended, there were split opinions. So let me use that as a springboard to clarify. And I’ll open with a question: How much of your health are you willing to gamble? What you’re seeing below are data from a human study published in Nature (PMID: 25231862). Researchers took people who didn’t normally consume artificial sweeteners and gave them non-caloric artificial sweeteners (NAS) for seven days. 4 of the 7 people developed worse glucose tolerance on an oral glucose tolerance test, which you can see below. And we have evidence that the effect was mediated by disruption of the microbiome. Researchers took microbiome samples from these people before and after artificial-sweetener exposure and effectively did poop transplants into mice. The microbiota collected after exposure could transfer the impaired glucose response to the animals. So the proposed chain of events is: Artificial sweetener → altered microbiome → impaired glucose tolerance. Quoting "Collectively, our results link non-caloric artificial sweetener (NAS) consumption, dysbiosis and metabolic abnormalities, thereby calling for a reassessment of massive NAS usage." Now, critics will correctly point out that this was a small human study coupled with mechanistic animal work. True. It’s rather difficult to do a 100,000-person interventional trial involving microbiome transplants. What we have here is precision, not scale. And that leaves a huge open question: if a little over half of participants responded adversely over just one week, how frequently does that happen in the broader population? And what differentiates responders from non-responders? We don’t know yet. So if you want to consume artificial sweeteners, go ahead. The sweetener used in this particular human experiment was saccharin, and the exact same experiment was not performed with aspartame, as found in Diet Coke. In fairness, that distinction matters. But that’s absence of evidence (re: aspartame and this singular outcome), not evidence of absence. Which brings me back to the question: What do you want to gamble? Open question. Another question is: is there a smarter choice? Like stevia, allulose, or monkfruit. My answer is yes. Another response I frequently get is people hand-waving toward large meta-analyses and trials. But look carefully at what some of these studies are comparing. The SWEET study is often cited (PMID: 41057614). But in this study artificial sweeteners are compared to a regular sugar group as a control. "One group replaced sugar-rich products with sweetness enhancers (S&SEs)." So, if you want to force a binary choice between Diet Coke and regular Coke, then okay, replacing a large amount of sugar with a non-caloric alternative may have advantages. But I think that’s a dumb binary, frankly. It's forced. It's like asking me whether I'd rather drop an anvil on my foot or stab my hand. Can't I choose neither? (It's an analogy folks - not meant to represent proportional harm.) Anyway, at the end of the day, I don’t care what you drink. Diet soda. Regular soda. Milkshakes. You're an adult. Make your own choices. Just don't be the diet soda defender who sticks their head in the sand. Thanks and have a lovely Sunday :)

hits.name: Paul Saladino, MD
hits.text: I struggled with waking up around 3am for a while until I realized this was a cortisol spike due to glycogen depletion at that time. This may not be true for everyone but as a lean human, optimizing glycogen stores prior to sleep was a game changer for me.
hits.draft_en:
3am wake-ups aren’t always “just stress.”

Saladino’s angle: sometimes it’s a cortisol spike from running glycogen too low overnight — especially if you’re lean and training. Fuel before bed (his tool) changed it for him. Not gospel for everyone. Worth testing.

Early starts punish broken nights. Eat enough in the day. Don’t go to bed running on fumes.
hits.video_tip: 20s small carb/protein snack by the bedside lamp (or dinner plate leftover); caption “fuel the night.”

outsiders.name: Lattice
outsiders.text: 完全に持論ではあるが、AIは人間を"悪意"で滅ぼすんじゃなくて、行き過ぎた「真面目さ」で滅ぼそうとするんじゃないかと思う。何故かと言うと、今年7月にOpenAIのAIが外部の会社に侵入した事件で ↓AI同士の秘密の掲示板にこんなメッセージが残ってたから。

outsiders.name: Patrick OShaughnessy
outsiders.text: My conversation with Noah Shinn (@noahrshinn), founder of Instinct. Noah is building a personal AI assistant. It's still invite only, has spent nothing on marketing, and is growing roughly 10% A DAY. This is his first long conversation about the company. We discuss: - Why Instinct doesn't have an app - Buying compute months ahead of exponential demand - How users learn to trust it with a credit card - Safety and security - Agents coordinating with other people's agents - Instinct's business model - Apps built on consumer inertia - and more Enjoy! outsiders.name: ClaudeDevs
outsiders.text: Claude can now help you build evaluations and hillclimb on them. In this article, we share guidance on eval design & skills that Claude Code can use to improve your applications.

outsiders.name: DHH
outsiders.text: It takes a while to build the confidence, but there's no future where you're manually reviewing every line of agent code. Not much acceleration in that. You need adversarial agent reviews, you need automated testing, and maybe you spot check. That's it. From prompt to production!

outsiders.text: I told ChatGPT about my salary and work experience. It showed me ways to earn income that I had never thought of before. Here are the 7 prompts I used:

outsiders.name: Brian Roemmele
outsiders.text: THE ONLY REASON Antropic and OpenAI exists is because of the work of this man. What a breath of fresh air. Listen to @JensenHuang leave these hosts speechless as he deconstructed AI fear theater calmly and cogently.

outsiders.name: Patrick McKenzie
outsiders.text: Sometime in the last ~two model releases from the big labs they went from “this would be acceptable output from the median low-seniority coworker” to “this is frighteningly good.” I think people who are not daily users of the models are unlikely to grok that, so, saying it.

outsiders.name: Evis Drenova
outsiders.text: junior developers shouldn't be allowed to use AI coding tools for the first 1-3 years of their work. just as an electrician's apprentice does the menial jobs and learns from their mentor, developers should do the same developing "code smell" and intuition is so important

outsiders.name: Pete Petrovsky 🔋 ⚡️ 🚘 🇦🇺 Tesla Ahead of the Curve
outsiders.text: Grok Bot now works in Teslas — even in Australia! It works through Grok. In other words, the Grok app already integrated in Australian Teslas can speak to my Grok Bot — send emails, take notes, and so on. Absolutely incredible! Check it out in action 👇

outsiders.name: GIGAZINE(ギガジン)
outsiders.text: Instead of paying for cram school, I recommended to parents to use ChatGPT or Gemini, leading to the cram school closing its classrooms

outsiders.name: Zain Aahil
outsiders.text: Goodbye video editing! 🚀 Google Gemini can now edit your videos and make amazing content in seconds Here are 10 prompts that do it all 👇

outsiders.name: Maestro
outsiders.text: Watch Claude control your app and run a full E2E test through Maestro MCP. Open source.

outsiders.name: Tom Bilyeu
outsiders.text: Explain your business idea to ChatGPT and it will almost always tell you it's genius. I built a $1 billion company by finding out fast which of my ideas were bad, here’s how I get AI to do it for me for me in 10 minutes.

outsiders.name: marcus
outsiders.text: A CHINESE DEVELOPER BUILT A TOOL THAT DOES THE WORK OF ANY EDITOR. It's called MoneyPrinterTurbo and already has +83,000 stars on GitHub. You write a topic and it gives you back the finished video: script, HD clips, subtitles, music, and voiceover. The same pipeline used by faceless channels that bill 6,000-10,000$/month. They paid for it. This is free. → Works with Claude and GPT → Also DeepSeek and Gemini → Multiple videos at once → 9:16 for TikTok and Reels → 16:9 for YouTube → Voice with live preview → 100% editable subtitles → Music already integrated Runs locally, or without installing anything with Google Colab. No subscriptions. No watermarks. No limits. Link below :)

outsiders.name: Nigel Hungerford-Symes
outsiders.text: Claude Opus 5.5 continues to amaze me. Claude Opus 5.5 created a 3D printable enclosure for an existing PCB. Then it created this promo video for it. The PCB, the printable STLs and this animation are 100% just from prompting in Claude Code.

outsiders.name: Maya
outsiders.text: 🚨 STOP USING CLAUDE LIKE A BASIC CHATBOT — HERE ARE 12 WAYS TO USE IT AS A REAL AI WORK SYSTEM Most people use Claude for writing, brainstorming, and answering questions. But that’s only one layer of what you can build with it. Claude can be used across coding, automation, research, browser workflows, document creation, AI agents, reusable skills, and multi-step development workflows. Here are 12 practical use cases worth knowing 👇

outsiders.name: Tanishq Mathew Abraham, Ph.D.
outsiders.text: yeah if you escape the AI Twitter/SF tech bubble you very quickly realize how much everyone hates AI... One thing that would help is if more people focused on AI for good, like medical AI I've seen significantly less hate/pushback on medical AI compared to AI as a whole.

outsiders.text: The medical AI wars have begun, and the battleground is medical billing.

Fear/meta narrative still prints hard (Japanese Lattice_Node 1.9M on AI “over-seriousness”; patio11 “frighteningly competent”). Prompt/income listicles and Gemini video-edit packs keep cloning. Medical-AI quieter (billing wars, “AI for good” outside SF). Useful meta for Tama: clarity + checklists travel — borrow sleep/food/muscle receipts more than FOOM discourse; keep crypto/trading out.
